closed.evidence: SpeleothemClusterFeature + LargeDripstoneFeature are 26.3 records vs 26.2 classes with a configuration object: place/placeColumn/getSpeleothemHeight/canPlacePool/replaceBlocksWithBaseBlocks/getChanceOfStalagmiteOrStalactite bodies are identical modulo this.x -> config.x() (config threaded as an extra parameter). LargeDripstoneFeature.place + isSuitableForWind follow the same pattern (config param). No behaviour change; the Rust ports the shared bodies.
Vanilla CommandEncoder is GPU plumbing (RenderPearl/Blaze3D command recording); the Rust uses wgpu::CommandEncoder and only mentions vanilla's in a comment. No port of the class exists.
GpuFormat/GpuFormat$ComponentType enum churn (values/init/componentType re-shaped); the Rust only cites GpuFormat.RGBA8_UNORM in a comment. No port of the enum.

BlendFunction record ctor/accessor re-shape (added/removed <init>/alpha/color, equals/hashCode/toString); every Rust mention is a doc citation (TRANSLUCENT/INVERT/ADDITIVE/OVERLAY) — no Rust code ports the record.

SectionRenderDispatcher (+RenderSectionBufferSlice record re-shape) and EntitySectionStorage changes are GPU/entity-section internals; the Rust only cites getStats/count in comments. No port of the changed methods.

ApplyBonusCount: only the condition form (Optional<Holder<LootItemCondition>> -> List<LootItemCondition>) and getOptional -> getOptionalParameter rename; run + the three bonus formulas byte-identical. MatchTool.test: the same rename only.

IcebergFeature is a 26.3 record vs a 26.2 Feature<BlockStateConfiguration> class; place takes a FeaturePlaceContext instead of direct args and reads the state from the config — the place body (sea-level origin, snowOnTop 0.7, shape angle/ellipse) is identical.

TrunkPlacer: the TreeFeature parameter becomes TreeConfiguration; provider access changes form (tree.trunkProvider().value() -> config.trunkProvider) with the same value; placeTrunk/placeLog/placeLogIfFree/placeBelowTrunkBlock bodies identical.

SpriteContents$AnimationState: RenderPearl -> Blaze3D import paths and setUniform -> bindTexture renames in drawToAtlas; close() byte-identical; AnimatedTexture.createAnimationState a signature re-shape. GPU plumbing only.

WaterloggedVegetationPatchFeature: ctor/config-class re-shape (26.3 record-style ctor vs 26.2 VegetationPatchConfiguration); placeGroundPatch/placeVegetation bodies identical modulo the config parameter threaded through the super calls. MultifaceSpreadeableBlock only gains a codec. Rust references are comments.
SectionMesh$SectionDraw record re-shape (init/indexType/equals/hashCode/toString); SectionMesh loses getCompileTaskStartTime, a timing getter. No Rust module ports either; no Rust surface.

CuboidItemModelWrapper: 26.3 pre-splits quads into ItemQuads and caches the animated flag at construction; 26.2 keeps the QuadCollection and calls prepareQuadList().addAll(quads.getAll()) + hasMaterialFlag(2) at update time — same quads submitted, same animated condition. LayerRenderState setQuads -> prepareQuadList rename. Rust references are doc comments.

Illusioner.performRangedAttack: 26.2 inlines the uncertainty as 14 - difficulty.getId()*4; 26.3 calls RangedAttackMob.rangedAttackUncertainty, whose default-method bytecode is exactly 14 - getDifficulty().getId()*4 — a pure extraction, no behaviour change. The Rust already uses (14 - difficulty.id*4). IllusionerRenderer.getBoundingBoxForCulling is a signature re-shape.

The entire ExperimentalRedstoneWireEvaluator diff is the RedstoneWireBlock -> RedStoneWireBlock class rename (26.2's name); calculateCurrentChanges, enqueueNeighborWire, isConnected, updatePowerStrength bodies identical.

ClientChunkCache$Storage section-emptiness methods (markSectionEmpty/NotEmpty removed, onChunkAdded/Removed/refreshEmptySections changed); the Rust only cites ClientChunkCache in a doc comment. No port of the storage.

WardenSpawnTrackerCommand: 26.3 tracker form vs 26.2 manual one/many branching, and getWardenSpawnTracker() returns Optional in 26.2 (ifPresent) vs direct in 26.3. Unobservable in the Rust: cmd_warden_spawn_tracker is single-player-only (always the .single message, tracker always present).
SnifferRenderer.getBoundingBoxForCulling added+removed (signature re-shape); the Rust only mentions the renderer in a comment.

ScreenNarrationCollector$Output: the NarrationTrigger field/ctor arg/accessor are 26.3-only; nest() is identical modulo dropping the trigger argument — the same removal item 129 already applied to the Rust. ScreenNarrationCollector.update is a signature re-shape.

FilePackResources$FileResourcesSupplier: openMetadata/openResources renamed openFull/openPrimary (internal supplier API); listResources/getResource unchanged; FilePackResources <init> only. Rust references are comments.

CategoryRuleEntry: 26.3 wraps the label in a FocusableTextWidget (focusable, border-on-focus); 26.2 draws centered text directly with an anonymous narratable and empty children(). The Rust draws centered text + a narratable region — the 26.2 form; no focus behaviour to remove.

EffectsChangedTrigger$TriggerInstance matches/validate/gotEffectsFrom changed, but effects.rs ports no trigger-matching logic (its only 'matches' is an EffectAction::Poison filter); the module is the HUD effects display, citing the trigger in one comment.

JigsawBlock gains a codec and canAttach changes; Pools.bootstrap changes. The Rust ports JigsawBlockEntity (name/target/pool/joint) and cites getFrontFacing; no can_attach exists in the module or the level placement code. Data bootstrap has no Rust surface.

TickCommand step/stopSprinting/stopStepping: 26.3 throws CommandSyntaxException (ERROR_TICK_STEP_NOT_FROZEN etc.); 26.2 sends sendFailure and returns — step returns 1 even on failure, both stops return 0 on failure. Ported cmd_tick: the three failure arms now call command_failure (red text, silent-aware) and return Ok(1)/Ok(0)/Ok(0). cargo check -p horizon-client clean (only the two pre-existing warnings).
GameModeSwitcherScreen, GameModeSlot and GameModeIcon decompile byte-identically in both versions; the extractSelection/extractSlot/extractBackground/<clinit> 'changed' flags are bytecode artifacts.
ReloadableResourceManager listResourceStacks/listResources added+removed (signature re-shape); the Rust only cites createReload in a comment.

SulfurCubeArchetype's only diff is the codec: items decodes via holderSet in 26.3, homogeneousList in 26.2 (same JSON lists); the Rust loads archetype items from tags, not the codec. SulfurCubeRenderer extractRenderState is GPU plumbing; the Rust cites its scale in a comment.
JsonRpcNotificationService worldUpgradeStarted/Progress/Finished/Failed are 26.3-only (removed in 26.2); the Rust only cites broadcastNotification in a comment. No port of the upgrade notifications.
StairBlock and BaseCoralPlantTypeBlock only gain codecs (+ <clinit>/lambda$static); the ported methods (getStairsShape, scanForWater, tryScheduleDieTick) are unchanged.
ResourceArgument gains getConfiguredFeature/getEntityType/getStructure in 26.3 (26.3-only accessors); the Rust only cites ResourceArgument in a comment.
CommandBlock only gains a codec (+ <clinit>/lambda$static); no behaviour method changed.

LightningBoltRenderer: 26.3 hoists the bolt colour (0.45/0.45/0.5) and the segment/layer/branch counts into constants and takes them as quad parameters in 26.2 — the call site passes 0.45F/0.45F/0.5F literally; quad bodies, random draws (nextInt(11)-5 offsets, 11/31 branch steps), layer/branch/segment loops identical.
DropExperienceBlock only gains a codec (+ <clinit>/lambda$static); no behaviour method changed. The Rust cites its XP ranges in a comment.

AbstractFurnaceMenu.isFuel: 26.3 checks DataComponents.COOKING_FUEL, 26.2 uses level.fuelValues().isFuel — the Rust's menu is_fuel already uses the FuelValues burn_time table (item 1's port). CraftingTableBlock only gains a codec.
LeashKnotRenderer.submit differs only by a null 8th argument to submitModel in 26.2 (signature difference); FenceBlock only gains a codec. GPU plumbing; Rust references are comments.

CuredZombieVillagerTrigger$TriggerInstance: the predicate type changes (Holder<LootItemCondition> in 26.3 vs ContextAwarePredicate in 26.2) and validateHolder -> validate, but matches() is the same three-predicate conjunction (player/zombie/villager), which the Rust already evaluates via adv::conditions.
CloseSpectatorItem, ScrollMenuItem and TeleportToPlayerMenuCategory extractIcon decompile identically in both versions; the 'changed' flags are bytecode artifacts.
FlowerBlock only gains a codec (+ <clinit>/lambda$static); suspiciousStewEffects/makeEffectList unchanged.
WeatheringCopperChestBlock only gains a codec (+ <clinit>/lambda$static); randomTick unchanged.

RedstoneTorchBlock.tick: 26.3 calls setBlockAndUpdate, 26.2 calls setBlock(pos, state, 3) — and setBlockAndUpdate IS setBlock(pos, state, 3) in both versions (established in item 414). Toggle/burnout logic otherwise identical.

TreeDecorator$Context.isReplaceable/isWaterOrWaterNearby are 26.3-only helpers (canBeReplaced check; water at/around pos); the only 26.3 caller in the whole treedecorators package is ShelfMushroomDecorator, which is 26.3-only (ShelfMushroomBlock absent in 26.2). No 26.2 decorator uses them and the Rust ports none of it.
BanNoticeScreens createNameBan/createSkinBan lambdas differ only by Blaze3D.openUri -> Util.getPlatform().openUri (the URI-opener move). Same links, same screens.
EffectsInInventory extractBackground/extractEffects decompile identically in both versions; the 'changed' flags are bytecode artifacts.
TestBlock only gains a codec (+ <clinit>); no behaviour method changed.
DebugEntryCategory and DebugScreenEntries decompile identically in both versions; the <clinit> 'changed' flags are bytecode artifacts (the registration lists are the same).
